vakbeschrijving.nl: This course integrates theory and skills obtained in other courses in a real-world field setting. You will discuss properties, processes and links between different parts of the Earth system in a field setting, based on your own observations and measurements. The course revolves around a trip along the Meuse river, between the Belgian Ardennes and the Dutch Limburg. Before the trip, you will prepare for the excursion by collecting information and analyzing data from the field area. In the field, you gain real-world experience with topics related to the subsurface, surface, water, (paleo)climate and weather, as well as with relevant measuring techniques. The field trip itself consists of two components. First, in an excursion-style field trip, you will learn to observe and measure various components of the Earth system through exercises at excursion stops. Then, in a group project, you will focus on acquiring data, e.g. river discharge, geophysical measurements, GNSS profiles and a LiDAR based DTM. After the field trip, you and your group will process, analyze, visualize and interpret this data, and present your findings to other groups in a poster session.

leerdoelen.nl:
1. Identify Earth system processes and properties based on field observations of the Earth’s subsurface, surface, water cycle, and atmosphere.

  1. Discuss relations between the Earth’s spheres based on field observations.

  1. Collect data in the field using various techniques and sensors, following HSE practices, to gain experience in the process of data collection and its challenges.

  1. Apply your processing, analysis, visualization and interpretation skills on field data to investigate Earth system processes or properties.

  1. Effectively communicate findings in a poster presentation.  

  1. Maintain a portfolio that demonstrates critical reflection on your personal and professional development.

toetsing.nl:
Formative assessment: 

Exercises at each excursion stop, feedback by teachers, also on personal notebook. 

Feedback on data collection and processing by teachers during fieldwork and in Q&A sessions after the fieldwork back in Delft. 

 

Summative assessment (incl. weights): 

50% Written exam. Questions related to the excursion stops. Students are allowed to use their own written notes made during the fieldwork, and the excursion guidebook. 

50% Poster presentation. 

Pass/fail: Portfolio. 

 

Resit of the written exam is a essay on a topic related to the field-excursion. 

Resit of the presentation is a repair option, where the student or group will be given additional tasks to improve on, depending on their previous work. The grade for the presentation repair is maximum 6.0.

toelichting_onderwijsmethode.nl:
Fieldwork preparation: lectures on background info for the fieldwork, HSE and social safety, field techniques; practical on field data and field techniques. 

 Fieldwork: the fieldwork will take about 6 days. Preliminary program:

  • 4 days will be spent on an excursion, with various exercises at the excursion stops about the subsurface, surface, water and atmosphere. Students should collect notes and data at the field sites that will be used for the written exam.  

  • 2 days are available for a data collection campaign in groups, in which students use several techniques to study an aspect of a valley at risk of river flooding (e.g. morphology, water discharge, ground water level, subsurface properties, weather system). 

 Fieldwork reporting: data collected in the field campaign will be analyzed during and after the fieldwork and presented in a pitch & poster presentation. Practicals / Q&A sessions will be offered for questions and feedback, and support in making a pitch and poster presentation. The groups collect complimentary datasets, and students are expected to attend each other’s posters.
